title: Strong Majority Edge-Coloring
summary: A strong majority edge-coloring of a graph is an edge-coloring in which, for every edge $e$ and every color $i$, at most half of the edges adjacent to $e$ have color $i$. Such a coloring exists only for graphs with no pendant path of length two, which, following Kalinowski, Kamyczura, Pilśniak, and Woźniak, we call admissible. They proved that every admissible graph admits such a coloring with at most eight colors and conjectured that four colors always suffice. We improve the upper bound from eight to five.
